neighbours.study: The Bible and the ancient Near East (32)

neighbours.siteTitle: Mesha and the world of Moab

1KI 14:25.text: In the fifth year of Rehoboam’s reign, Shishak king of Egypt came up and attacked Jerusalem.

notes: Hebrew the River; also in verse 24
1KI 4:21.text: And Solomon reigned over all the kingdoms from the Euphrates to the land of the Philistines, as far as the border of Egypt. These kingdoms offered tribute and served Solomon all the days of his life.

notes: Hebrew; LXX four hundred and fortieth
Ziv was the second month of the ancient Hebrew lunar calendar, usually occurring within the months of April and May; also in verse 37.
1KI 6:1.text: In the four hundred and eightieth year after the Israelites had come out of the land of Egypt, in the month of Ziv, the second month of the fourth year of Solomon’s reign over Israel, he began to build the house of the LORD.

notes: Hebrew the Millo; also in verse 24
1KI 9:15.text: This is the account of the forced labor that King Solomon imposed to build the house of the LORD, his own palace, the supporting terraces, and the wall of Jerusalem, as well as Hazor, Megiddo, and Gezer.

1KI 9:16.text: Pharaoh king of Egypt had attacked and captured Gezer. He had set it on fire, killed the Canaanites who lived in the city, and given it as a dowry to his daughter, Solomon’s wife.

1SA 13:19.text: And no blacksmith could be found in all the land of Israel, because the Philistines had said, “The Hebrews must not be allowed to make swords or spears.”

1SA 17:1.text: Now the Philistines gathered their forces for war at Socoh in Judah, and they camped between Socoh and Azekah in Ephes-dammim.

notes: LXX; Hebrew of Gai; that is, of the valley
1SA 17:52.text: Then the men of Israel and Judah charged forward with a shout and pursued the Philistines to the entrance of Gath and to the gates of Ekron. And the bodies of the Philistines were strewn along the Shaaraim road to Gath and Ekron.

1SA 1:3.text: Year after year Elkanah would go up from his city to worship and sacrifice to the LORD of Hosts at Shiloh, where Eli’s two sons, Hophni and Phinehas, were priests to the LORD.

1SA 4:11.text: The ark of God was captured, and Eli’s two sons, Hophni and Phinehas, died.

2SA 5:11.text: Now Hiram king of Tyre sent envoys to David, along with cedar logs, carpenters, and stonemasons, and they built a palace for David.

2SA 5:7.text: Nevertheless, David captured the fortress of Zion (that is, the City of David).

2SA 5:9.text: So David took up residence in the fortress and called it the City of David. He built it up all the way around, from the supporting terraces inward.

2TI 3:16.text: All Scripture is God-breathed and is useful for instruction, for conviction, for correction, and for training in righteousness,

notes: Succoth means booths or shelters or tabernacles.
EXO 12:37.text: The Israelites journeyed from Rameses to Succoth with about 600,000 men on foot, besides women and children.

notes: MT; SP in Canaan and Egypt; LXX in Egypt and Canaan
EXO 12:40.text: Now the duration of the Israelites’ stay in Egypt was 430 years.

EXO 12:41.text: At the end of the 430 years, to the very day, all the LORD’s divisions went out of the land of Egypt.

EXO 1:11.text: So the Egyptians appointed taskmasters over the Israelites to oppress them with forced labor. As a result, they built Pithom and Rameses as store cities for Pharaoh.

EXO 6:16.text: These were the names of the sons of Levi according to their records: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari. Levi lived 137 years.

EXO 6:17.text: The sons of Gershon were Libni and Shimei, by their clans.

EXO 6:18.text: The sons of Kohath were Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel. Kohath lived 133 years.

EXO 6:19.text: The sons of Merari were Mahli and Mushi. These were the clans of the Levites according to their records.

EXO 6:20.text: And Amram married his father’s sister Jochebed, and she bore him Aaron and Moses. Amram lived 137 years.

GAL 3:17.text: What I mean is this: The law that came 430 years later does not revoke the covenant previously established by God, so as to nullify the promise.

GEN 15:13.text: Then the LORD said to Abram, “Know for certain that your descendants will be strangers in a land that is not their own, and they will be enslaved and mistreated four hundred years.

GEN 15:16.text: In the fourth generation your descendants will return here, for the iniquity of the Amorites is not yet complete.”

notes: Hebrew; LXX the nine sons, probably including Joseph’s grandsons through Ephraim and Manasseh; see 1 Chronicles 7:14–29.
Hebrew (see also Exodus 1:5); LXX (see also Acts 7:14) seventy-five
GEN 46:27.text: And with the two sons who had been born to Joseph in Egypt, the members of Jacob’s family who went to Egypt were seventy in all.

GEN 47:11.text: So Joseph settled his father and brothers in the land of Egypt and gave them property in the best part of the land, the district of Rameses, as Pharaoh had commanded.

JDG 11:26.text: For three hundred years Israel has lived in Heshbon, Aroer, and their villages, as well as all the cities along the banks of the Arnon. Why did you not take them back during that time?

JDG 18:31.text: So they set up for themselves Micah’s graven image, and it was there the whole time the house of God was in Shiloh.

JDG 1:27.text: At that time Manasseh failed to drive out the inhabitants of Beth-shean, Taanach, Dor, Ibleam, Megiddo, and their villages; for the Canaanites were determined to dwell in that land.

JDG 1:28.text: When Israel became stronger, they pressed the Canaanites into forced labor, but they never drove them out completely.

JDG 1:29.text: Ephraim also failed to drive out the Canaanites living in Gezer; so the Canaanites continued to dwell among them in Gezer.

JDG 1:30.text: Zebulun failed to drive out the inhabitants of Kitron and Nahalol; so the Canaanites lived among them and served as forced laborers.

JDG 1:31.text: Asher failed to drive out the inhabitants of Acco, Sidon, Ahlab, Achzib, Helbah, Aphik, and Rehob.

JDG 1:32.text: So the Asherites lived among the Canaanite inhabitants of the land, because they did not drive them out.

JDG 1:33.text: Naphtali failed to drive out the inhabitants of Beth-shemesh and Beth-anath. So the Naphtalites also lived among the Canaanite inhabitants of the land, but the inhabitants of Beth-shemesh and Beth-anath served them as forced laborers.

JDG 1:34.text: The Amorites forced the Danites into the hill country and did not allow them to come down into the plain.

JDG 1:35.text: And the Amorites were determined to dwell in Mount Heres, Aijalon, and Shaalbim. But when the house of Joseph grew in strength, they pressed the Amorites into forced labor.

JDG 21:19.text: “But look,” they said, “there is a yearly feast to the LORD in Shiloh, which is north of Bethel east of the road that goes up from Bethel to Shechem, and south of Lebonah.”

JDG 2:7.text: And the people served the LORD throughout the days of Joshua and of the elders who outlived him, who had seen all the great works that the LORD had done for Israel.

JDG 4:2.text: So the LORD sold them into the hand of Jabin king of Canaan, who reigned in Hazor. The commander of his forces was Sisera, who lived in Harosheth-hagoyim.

JER 7:12.text: But go now to the place in Shiloh where I first made a dwelling for My Name, and see what I did to it because of the wickedness of My people Israel.

JOS 11:10.text: At that time Joshua turned back and captured Hazor and put its king to the sword, because Hazor was formerly the head of all these kingdoms.

JOS 11:13.text: Yet Israel did not burn any of the cities built on their mounds, except Hazor, which Joshua burned.

JOS 15:36.text: Shaaraim, Adithaim, and Gederah (or Gederothaim)—fourteen cities, along with their villages.

JOS 6:24.text: Then the Israelites burned up the city and everything in it. However, they put the silver and gold and articles of bronze and iron into the treasury of the LORD’s house.

JOS 8:28.text: So Joshua burned Ai and made it a permanent heap of ruins, a desolation to this day.

JOS 8:30.text: At that time Joshua built an altar on Mount Ebal to the LORD, the God of Israel,

JOS 8:31.text: just as Moses the servant of the LORD had commanded the Israelites. He built it according to what is written in the Book of the Law of Moses: “an altar of uncut stones on which no iron tool has been used.” And on it they offered burnt offerings to the LORD, and they sacrificed peace offerings.

PSA 78:60.text: He abandoned the tabernacle of Shiloh, the tent He had pitched among men.
